audit.whatIsWrong: Row 1 read Renekton while its why says 'Level 2 stays even as neither of you can open a committed trade yet'. Row 3 read Skill while its why says 'your Q and E are online and you can disengage his stun, tilting it your way'. Row 6 read Renekton while its why says 'your sustain and stats catch his falloff, leveling the duel back out'.
audit.why: Renekton owns level 3 and the first-item window and nothing else; level 2 is pre-Fury and two items is where a falloff bully loses the duel. The packet chart reads Skill / Skill / Renekton / Zaahen / Skill / Renekton / Skill, and the mirror audit already committed to exactly those three flips.
audit.corrected: Row 1 to Skill, row 3 to Zaahen, row 6 to Skill, all as matched full/content pairs. Rows 2 and 5 stay Renekton.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-3 spike said 'full fury' without the threshold or what changes at it, and the level-6 entry called Zaahen's ultimate 'R Final Retribution'.
audit.why: Riot's text puts the breakpoint at more than 50 Fury: below it Ruthless Predator stuns 0.75s, above it he slashes three times, stuns 1.5s and DESTROYS damage shields on the target. That is a doubled stun plus shield removal on one bar you can read. Zaahen's R has no name in the kit file; what it does have is a heal for a portion of the damage dealt on 110s.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] rewritten on the 50-Fury threshold with both stun durations and the shield destruction; spikes[1] rewritten on the R heal and the 16s W gap; fabricated names removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'E Golden Onslaught' and 'R Final Retribution' are fabricated. Cull the Meek's heal was mentioned once as 'sustain' with no anti-heal instruction anywhere in the prose, and Ruthless Predator's auto-attack reset was never mentioned.
audit.why: Cull the Meek is a flat 7s that heals off every target hit and heals more above 50 Fury — it is the mechanic that refunds every extended trade, so Grievous Wounds timing decides them. Ruthless Predator also resets his auto, so the wind-up rather than the cast is the step-back cue. Renekton's Fury generation increases when he is LOW, so a losing Renekton is more dangerous, not less.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal written into spikes[3] and breakdown.cooldowns; the Fury-when-low read stated in spikes[0]; W and E cooldowns (16s at rank 1 each) added to spikes[1], mid, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t; fabricated names replaced with slot references.

audit.why: report[8].t already calls early Oblivion Orb / Executioner's, which is the right answer to Cull the Meek.

edits.before: Renekton's level 3 is his hardest window — with full fury he chains Cull the Meek (Q) heal, Ruthless Predator (W) stun and a Slice-and-Dice (E) dash to burst you before your Q Darkin Glaive and E Golden Onslaught can answer, so respect his empowered W.
edits.after: Renekton's level 3 is his hardest window — above 50 Fury he chains the Cull the Meek (Q) heal, a Ruthless Predator (W) that stuns 1.5s instead of 0.75s and destroys shields, and the Slice and Dice (E) dash. Read his Fury bar, not his health bar.

edits.before: At 6 your R Final Retribution gives you an all-in he can't cleanly out-trade, and by 4-5 your own combo has come online — hold your E Golden Onslaught to disengage his W stun and the lane starts evening back toward you.
edits.after: At 6 your R gives you an all-in he cannot cleanly out-trade, and it heals you for part of the damage it deals. His W is 16s at rank 1 — hold your E to disengage that stun, then commit inside the gap it leaves.

edits.before: By two items you catch and pass him — Renekton is a falloff bully, so once your sustain and stats are up his empowered combo stops one-shotting the trade and side-lane duels go even to yours.
edits.after: By two items you catch and pass him — Renekton is a falloff bully. Keep Grievous Wounds up: Cull the Meek is a 7s heal that grows with Fury, and it is what refunds every extended trade he takes.

edits.before: His level 3 with empowered Ruthless Predator (W) stun is his best moment and he wins that window; but by 4-5 your Q Darkin Glaive and E Golden Onslaught come online and at 6 your R Final Retribution lets you answer his all-in.
edits.after: His level 3 with an empowered Ruthless Predator is his best moment and he wins that window; by 4-5 your Q and E come online and at 6 your R answers his all-in. His W is 16s at rank 1 — that gap is where you trade.

edits.before: Save E Golden Onslaught to dodge his Slice dash-in and stun
edits.after: Save your E dash to dodge his Slice and Dice and the stun

edits.before: - Renekton Ruthless Predator: matchup-defining — Empowered = long stun. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Ruthless Predator (W): matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1; above 50 Fury it stuns 1.5s and destroys shields. - Cull the Meek (Q): a 7s heal — anti-heal beats it. - Slice and Dice (E): 16s at rank 1.

edits.before: Empowered = long stun. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Empowered it stuns 1.5s and eats shields — engage after its 16s.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Above 50 Fury it stuns twice as long and destroys your shields.

edits.before: Track Renekton's Ruthless Predator (Stun): Empowered = long stun. Dodge it. When it is down — Combo + R him.
edits.after: Ruthless Predator: a 0.75s stun, or 1.5s and shield-destroying at 50+ Fury. It is 16s at rank 1.

notes: Renekton's W destroying damage shields matters more than usual for Zaahen because Sterak's Gage is in report[8].t as a core item — an empowered W removes it outright. I did not write that into the item text because report[8].t is otherwise correct and the sentence would not fit the band; worth a hand addition. Zaahen's Q, E and R are referred to by slot, matching this matchup's mirror auditor, who explicitly declined the missing-interactions names as an unconfirmed second source.
